blocks.text: Shimmering underwater images of shellfish suspended in shifting currents and spectral nocturnal scenes lend this film an almost otherworldly beauty, as though moments from science fiction had surfaced within everyday life. With a contemplative rhythm and patient gaze, Jessica Johnson and Ryan Ermacora expand our perception of space and time, gently unsettling familiar ways of seeing and revealing the hidden transformations of the landscape.

blocks.text: Set in the remote highlands of Montenegro, this year’s Sundance World Documentary Prize winner reflects on the fragile coexistence between ancestral knowledge and the growing pressures of the contemporary world.
In this visually arresting film, solo caretakers keep the fires burning in a remote Alpine chalet where weary hikers find modest lodgings.
Carl Sagan: We Are Made of Star Stuff
This awe-inspiring documentary is a detailed and thought-provoking portrait of the astronomer and astrophysicist behind Cosmos and Contact.
